#192 fix r5.summary:
Round 5 is amended into one commit, d08e2004, on main 8428e16c. Nothing was pushed. Both 3.13-only failure sets had product causes, and I fixed both.

(1) Windows py3.13, 47 failures: Python 3.13's ntpath.isabs requires a drive. ntpath.isabs('/opt/bin/uv') is True on 3.11/3.12 and False on 3.13. The 47 failures were test fixtures that used POSIX literals. They now build native absolute paths (_FAKE_UV etc.). The product also asked os.path.isabs in five places in cli/extension_install.py: the uv_path constructor, the which() lookup, PIP_CONFIG_FILE, UV_CONFIG_FILE and --index-url. So on Windows a drive-less rooted path meant different things on 3.12 and 3.13. All five now use _is_absolute_path, which requires a drive or UNC share and gives 3.13's answer on every interpreter.

(2) Ubuntu py3.13, 2 failures: a real process-tree leak, not a race. CPython gh-119710, in 3.13.15+ and 3.14, makes Process.wait() resolve when the child exits instead of when all its pipes close. Two places spent their grace period on wait() and skipped the hard kill when it resolved: the hook timeout ladder and the delegation reaper. The fix is a new aelix_ai.utils._process_tree.wait_released(), which restores the old meaning. Both grace periods now wait on it. Local 3.13.13 and 3.13.14 lack gh-119710, which is why rounds 1-4 passed locally. Attempt 2 of CI run 37760507281 failed the same 2 and the same 47 tests, so neither set is flaky.

New pins: tests/asyncio_exit_wait.py emulates gh-119710 on any interpreter. The two CI-failing cases now run under both wait() behaviours, plus a new timed-out-hook case and test_wait_released.py. Two new Windows path-rule tests run under Windows path semantics on any host. Docs: ADR-0238 and ADR-0241 amendments, the ADR-0241 index row, CHANGELOG (2 entries), the private-catalog guide and its bundled copy. Citations: 15 anchors relocated.

Whole suite after the fixes: Linux 3.13.15 (Docker, --init) 14354 passed / 0 failed; macOS 3.13.13 14347 passed / 0 failed; macOS 3.12.13, run last, 14347 passed / 0 failed. Full detail is in .omc/probes/192-live/r5/msg_r5.txt (REVIEW ROUND 5).

blocking.title: wait_released is stricter than pre-3.13.15 wait(): the hook ladder changed on every interpreter, while CHANGELOG/ADR-0238/docstrings say it restores the old meaning
blocking.detail: Before gh-119710, asyncio _wait() returned at once if _returncode was already set; pipe-gating applied only to a waiter registered before the exit. In run_hook_subprocess, when the shell has already exited at the timeout (it backgrounded a helper that keeps the hook's stdout/stderr, so communicate() never sees EOF), the old code skipped the soft signal, wait() returned at once, and the helper survived. HEAD waits on the pipes, the 1.0 s grace runs out, and hard_kill kills the helper. That is a user-visible change on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13.13-14 too. Arguably right under ADR-0238, but it is unpinned and contradicted by the CHANGELOG ('as it did before 3.13.15', 'On Python 3.13.15 and later'), the ADR-0238 #192 amendment, the wait_released docstring, the subprocess_hooks comment and the commit message. The reaper is unaffected (its waiter is registered while returncode is None). Fix: state the change in those texts (and next to 'a hook is allowed to background a helper'), and add a row (shell exits at once, helper keeps the pipes, timeout -> helper dead) that is red on 8428e16c on every interpreter. Or narrow it if the owner wants such helpers kept.
